climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Seasons this cool ripen Müller-Thurgau, Pinot Gris, Gewürztraminer and Riesling fully without cooking off their freshness.

soil.rock: Shale and mudstone are fine-grained rocks that hold heat well and are moderately fertile. Limestone makes alkaline soil that drains well yet can hold water for the vines. It is usually planted to grapes valued for their acidity. Loess is fine, wind-blown silt. Fertile and warm, it holds water well but drains poorly.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: The high ground runs about 2°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.
